kitDescription: Isabel is an Electric shotgun Attacker on Burst III who builds a personal "Marked Target" stage every time she fires her own burst. Her first burst gives herself +6.26% Critical Rate for 45 seconds, her second adds +18.03% Critical Damage, and her third adds +17.28% ATK — each stage keeps the earlier ones, and since the buffs last 45 seconds against a 40-second burst cooldown, all three stay up permanently once she reaches stage 3 (around her third burst). Separately, a passive skill drops a single 170.58%-of-ATK hit on the highest-defence enemies roughly every 15 seconds all fight long, independent of her burst. Her burst deals 149.85% of ATK to all enemies, and its payload grows with her Marked Target stage: stage 1 also puts a 39.96% Damage Taken debuff on the boss for 5 seconds (which lifts the whole team's damage), stage 2 adds a 299.7% hit, and stage 3 adds a further 349.65% hit on top. The catch is that her burst also shortens Full Burst by 5 seconds for every ally — a genuine team downside that trades window length for a faster rotation.

redAssertions: NONE on encoding: 21 passed / 2 skipped (the 2 skips are the blind's own multi-enemy GAP skips) / 0 failed vs the driver's shipped override.

ONE blind assertion was RETIRED, not flipped: the blind test additionally claimed the NET SIGN of 'Full Burst Duration ▼5 sec' (that removing it RAISES team damage). It fails against the shipped override because in this engine the shortener is a net BENEFIT (faster burst re-cycle dominates the shorter +50% window). This is not a kit line and not an encoding claim — it is the driver's own documented UNVERIFIED ⚑ blast-radius. Retiring it (rather than flipping it green) is the correct call; asserting either sign would fabricate a verdict on an unmeasured rotation quantity.

Schema adaptations only (ov.<slot> array shape, slug-keyed damage/burstCast events, 0-based casterIdx vs 1-based position, self-cast constraint on selfBuffs, CF-C dropping the escalating STEP instead of a top-level buff) — scaffolding, no assertion substance changed. Note: strictly UNMODIFIED the blind file does not compile against the real schema, so the mechanical convergence check is on the reconciled file; every substantive assertion survives reconciliation intact.

gotchas.summary: Crit-eligibility of the three burst-bucket damage instances (149.85 / 299.7 / 349.65) is neither set explicitly nor pinned by any test, and the driver's override note asserts the nuke is 'no crit' — which contradicts the formula SSOT. UNRESOLVED BY INSPECTION; needs a one-line check, not a code change on faith.
gotchas.evidence: Kit: 'Deals 149.85% of final ATK as Burst Skill damage' + 'Deals 299.7%/349.65% … as additional damage'. SSOT damage-calculation.md §1b table: 'burst nuke: crit ✅'; §2b: function-type instances 'CRIT at the caster's rate (default on)'. DRIVER: the three burst flatDamage effects carry no crit field, and the note reads '(burstCast, FB-exempt auto, no crit)'. BLIND S6: sets crit:true on all four flatDamage effects with the caveat 'Riders set crit:true (they crit at the caster's sheet rate)'. TWO BRANCHES, and the packet cannot settle which: (a) if the engine's flatDamage default is crit-ON, the omission is inert and only the note's 'no crit' wording is wrong — supported by the fact that the driver's S2 blocks also omit noRange yet the test still reads rangeApplied false and coreEligible false, i.e. the engine applies function-damage defaults on its own; (b) if the default is crit-OFF, all three burst instances are under-credited by roughly the full Major crit term (~14-15% of her burst payload once MT1/MT2 stack crit rate 6.26 and crit damage 18.03 onto her sheet). Neither the driver's 18 tests nor the S5 blind test asserts critEligible on ANY burst-bucket event, so no artifact discriminates the branches. Compounding note drift: the same note calls S2's crit:true a 'per-DoT opt-in' against a 'DOT_CRIT default OFF' global — stale framing left over from the pre-2026-07-20 dot encoding, and DOT_CRIT has been default ON since 2026-07-21.
gotchas.suggestedFix: Add one assertion to scripts/tests/units/isabel.test.ts pinning critEligible on the burst-bucket 149.85 / 299.7 / 349.65 events (mirroring the existing S2 critEligible pin). If it reads TRUE, delete the '(… no crit)' clause from the override note — the encoding is already faithful and nothing else changes. If it reads FALSE, add crit:true to the three burst flatDamage effects, since the SSOT states burst-skill and function damage crit at the caster's rate. Also drop the stale 'global DOT_CRIT default stays OFF' sentence from the note. NO magnitude is being proposed either way — this is a routing flag, not a tuned number.

verdictRationale: GO. All 10 gradeable kit clauses land FAITHFUL or DOCUMENTED_GAP (9 faithful encodings + the 5-highest-DEF-enemies clause, which both agents independently collapsed to the single partless boss and both documented). Convergence is mechanical and GREEN: the S5 blind test, written from prose alone against a redacted schema, runs 21 pass / 2 legitimate GAP skips / 0 fails against the driver's SHIPPED override, and its independent instruments (the monotone per-cast burst-payload ladder from damage totals; CF-C proving the Damage Taken debuff lifts TEAMMATES, not just Isabel; the casterAtkPct-absent and critRateNormalPct-absent scope pins; the burstCast-vs-fullBurstEnter trigger split, which is LIVE here because co-B3 helm gives the team 13 Full Bursts against Isabel's 7 casts) all corroborate the driver rather than merely echoing it. The one blind assertion that does not pass — that removing the ▼5s Full Burst shortening RAISES team damage — was RETIRED, not flipped, and that is the correct call: it asserts a net rotation SIGN that is this unit's documented unverified ⚑, and in this engine the shortener is actually a net benefit; asserting either direction would fabricate a verdict on an unmeasured quantity. The most valuable cross-check runs the other way and vindicates the driver: the blind S6 override gated the three burst riders on trigger burstCast{stage:1/2/3}, believing stage meant the Nth activation, when in this engine it is the burst TIER — for a Burst III unit that encoding would have fired ONLY the 349.65% rider and silently dropped both the 39.96% Damage Taken debuff and the 299.7% hit. The blind model flagged the risk itself and named the single-escalating-block alternative, which is exactly what the driver shipped; that is a RECON_ERROR, not a finding. Nothing is silently dropped (unmodeled is empty in all three slots and correctly so), every modelled line demonstrably FIRES at prose-implied cadence over 180s (S1 7 casts, S2 12 hits at t=0+15s, burst riders 7/6/5, FB shortening on 7 of 13 windows), and every load-bearing assertion has a named counterfactual that turns it RED — including the two nearest-wrongs most likely to be gotten wrong here (the collapsed 'all stages every cast' ladder and a sign-flipped fullBurstExtend). ONE unresolved item, ranked first and the owner's spot-check: no artifact in this packet pins crit-eligibility on the three burst-bucket damage instances, and the driver's note calls the nuke 'no crit' while the formula SSOT says burst nuke and function damage crit at the caster's rate. I could not settle it by inspection — if the engine's flatDamage default is crit-on (as the parallel noRange/coreEligible defaults suggest) it is inert note-wording; if not, her burst payload is under-credited by the full Major crit term. It is a one-assertion check, does not touch any kit line's structure, and does not block GO. Same-model residual to be aware of: S5/S6/S7 are all claude-opus-5, so their agreement proves stability rather than correctness; the genuinely cross-family signal here is the claude-fable-5 S2b review, which converged on all 9 lines with a single FIX watch-flag (the ▼5s line) that the shipped override already satisfies. The remaining standing ⚑ are unchanged and correctly documented, not asserted: the fullBurstExtend:-5 net rotation sign, the SG cadence tuple (pullsPerSec / reloadFrames 133 / rolling reload), and the unmodelled possibility of an in-game Marked-Target reset on the 45s expiry (inert here, since 45s > her 40s cooldown).
